h.select_rule: Choose 10 that together cover the most distinct mechanisms, edit fields and condition fields; prefer clear, falsifiable claims that go beyond well-known findings yet have a concrete mechanistic rationale; include both directions; drop near-duplicates and claims merely restating main effects.
h.strategy: Use the retrieved literature to identify what is already well established about main effects, then deliberately go one step further: propose conditional effects the literature implies but does not directly test, or where findings conflict. Draw on general mechanisms such as redundancy, bottlenecks, saturation, interference between components and compensation. Span many different edit and condition fields, propose some LOWER-direction hypotheses where a common edit is predicted to help less, and make each 'why' specific enough that a single comparison could refute it.

hyps.why: Replacing a 'none' on edge 0 reconnects node 1 and all of its downstream edges, so the gain exceeds that of swapping one live op for another.
With edge 0 removed, node 1 has no input, so a conv on edge 2 does nothing.
Node 2 output is never used when edge 5 is 'none', so conv on edge 1 is wasted.
With edge 5 removed, the skip on edge 3 is a key gradient path and its marginal value rises.
A strong conv path on edge 5 already supplies the output signal, so the direct skip on edge 3 adds less.
Capacity at the output node saturates when edge 4 already carries a 3x3 conv.
A second 3x3 conv into node 3 has diminishing returns when edge 5 is already one.
Feature extraction from the input saturates when edge 0 is already a 3x3 conv.
Deleting the identity shortcut hurts more than deleting other ops on that edge because it is a key gradient path.
Replacing a parameter-free pool with a learnable conv gains more than replacing an existing 3x3 conv.
